findings.title: Materials' 65-point lens gap signals earnings rebound
findings.body: Materials' trailing P/E sits at the 89th percentile while its forward P/E is at the 23rd, a 65-point divergence—the widest in the table. That spread implies the market is pricing in a 127 percent earnings surge, an aggressive bet that recent margin compression is about to reverse sharply.

findings.title: Consumer Staples' month-long de-rating hits extreme
findings.body: Consumer Staples' forward percentile plunged 39 points in a month, the steepest decline among all sectors, yet its forward P/E of 19.11 remains near the middle of its five-year range. This suggests the market is rapidly repricing defensive growth lower, but the multiple has not yet caught up to the speed of the sentiment shift.

findings.title: Real Estate's collapse belies stable earnings outlook
findings.body: Real Estate's forward percentile dropped 49 points in a month to the 8th percentile, yet its implied earnings growth is only a 4 percent decline. The valuation compression appears driven by multiple de-rating rather than deteriorating fundamentals, leaving the sector priced for a downturn that earnings estimates do not yet reflect.
